FINDING 0 (highest severity) — DIVERGENCE with BOTH backends exiting 0: the JS
backend answers 8 for every `sizeof`.

FILE: js_sizeof_always_8.zen.txt
CMD:  ./zen run tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/js_sizeof_always_8.zen.txt
OUT:  4
      1
      4
      1                        rc 0     (correct)
CMD:  ./zen emit-js tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/js_sizeof_always_8.zen.txt | node
OUT:  8
      8
      8
      8                        rc 0     (wrong, and silently so)

Both backends run to completion and exit 0 and disagree about what a valid
program means. By the campaign's own ranking this is priority 1.

ROOT CAUSE: bootstrap/zenrt.js:57
        const sizeof = (_name) => 8;   // element sizes unused on the print
                                       // path; DEFERRED for typed slices
      The emitter (src/compiler/backend/js/js_expr.zen:455 js_sizeof) faithfully
      emits `__zr.sizeof("i32")`; the runtime throws the name away. It is a
      KNOWN-deferred stub — but it is deferred as a WRONG ANSWER instead of as a
      JS-UNSUPPORTED refusal, so it produces silently wrong arithmetic rather
      than a diagnostic. Non-generic `sizeof(i32)` is affected too, so this is
      not confined to monomorphisation.

FOUND IN THE REAL CORPUS, not by the generator: a full C-vs-JS differential over
      tests/fixtures/zen/*.zen + examples/*.zen flagged
      tests/fixtures/zen/generic_literal_pin.zen —
        C  : 8 8 8 8 4 8 4 1 255
        JS : 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 255
      reduced to the four lines above. tools/fuzz-diff.zen cannot find it: its
      grammar never emits `sizeof`.

BLAST RADIUS: `sizeof` is how Zen computes allocation sizes and slice strides,
      so on the JS backend every `n * sizeof(T)` allocation is wrong for any T
      that is not 8 bytes wide. This is the plausible cause of several of the
      JS-RUNTIME-FAIL fixtures in the same sweep (hmap_*, btree_*).

CLASS: miscompile (C/JS divergence, both exit 0).
